injuries.description: It shown mild left knee effusion, small medial meniscus tear and swollen anterior cruciate ligament at his left knee joint.

injuries.icd_description: Injury to multiple structures of knee

injuries.description: The Plaintiff had a slip and fall on 7 November 2003 and suffered from an avulsion fracture of right distal tibia.

injuries.description: the Plaintiff may have sustained injury at his left shoulder, it was fully recovered soon after the 2nd Accident.

injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

manifestations.description: Persistent bilateral knee pain; such pain is pulsatile in character and is fluctuating in intensity. The left knee is more severe than the right side. There is resting pain and the pain increased with standing and walking.
Right ankle pain on weight bearing since right ankle sprain injury in late November 2003.
Persistent left shoulder pain which is more severe than the knee pain. It disturbs his sleep.
Numbness over the whole of left upper limb and ulnar half of right and index fingers.
On and off neck pain for about a year. It increases with movement.
Pain over left scapular and upper back.
Have to use stick for ambulation due to knee pain.
Walking tolerance is 10 minutes with the aid of a stick.
limitation of neck movement, left shoulder joint movement and left knee joints movement.

treatments_received: tapping of the effusion from the left knee (about 20 to 30 cc of clear fluid yielded)
23 sessions of physiotherapy commencing 15 February 2002 and last on 5 July 2002

losses.description: Have to use stick for ambulation; walking tolerance reduced; limping gait; difficulty walking up and down stairs/slope; cannot squat.
Unable to cope with his pre-accident job which required manual lifting of steel bars, continuous standing and squatting, climbing up and down and bilateral pulling and pushing.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Pain and limitation affecting activities such as walking tolerance and exercises recommended by physiotherapist.
